about: Generated from each pages/tool-*.md front matter; tools and libraries are separated by kind.

states.working: does its job end to end; its gates pass and are linked
states.early: usable, incomplete, with its limitations named
states.planned: a repository and a subdomain, not yet usable

paper.title: The Web-CLI: Verifiable Privacy for Tools, Models, and Inference Engines in the Browser

audits.title: rig: how to verify zero egress, asserted by its test suite

example.title: ImageMagick in a tab: sepia on a 480 by 320 PNG, nothing uploaded

shots.alt: magick-webCLI after a sepia run: the input gradient on the left, the sepia-toned output on the right, and the log line 'Done: sepia 80%'.

example.requests: 14 requests during page load and the run: 9 to magick.webcli.app, 3 to cdnjs.cloudflare.com (icon font), 2 to cdn.jsdelivr.net (ImageMagick WebAssembly). All were GETs and none carried a body, so the image was in no request.
example.verify: Open DevTools, Network, then drop an image and press Process.
example.note: magick now exposes URL runs for conversion and operations; the worked example remains the interactive measurement.

thumb.alt: 3mf-webCLI: a 3D model preview and multi-material printing controls.

line.out: a 3MF with its materials segmented by colour, for multi-material printing

not.why: bakes motion into an animated GLB; this converts one model to one print format and animates nothing

tools.limits: GLB input only. URL runs export 3MF; the interactive editor can also export segmented GLB. No gate table yet.

params.name: src
params.description: GLB URL to load with a credential-free GET.

params.name: run
params.description: Segment and export 3MF without a click.

params.name: materials
params.description: Fixed material count; omitted for auto-detection.

params.name: download
params.description: Also download the generated 3MF.

result.shape: { ok, op: 'convert', artifact: { mime, name, size, dataUrl } | null, error: string | null, meta: { tool, materials } }

tools.boundary: No uploads, no servers - all processing happens locally in your browser.
tools.name: 3mf

line.in: Markdown pages and optional posts in a GitHub repository
line.out: a static website committed back to that repository, with a feed when it has posts

not.why: makes the video releases a post can embed; this one encodes no video

tools.limits: Publishing is a commit to your repository, so it is egress, and it is yours to start. Its own test suite had 5 failures of 598 on 2026-11-15. Every page it generates loads Font Awesome from cdnjs, with no way to turn that off.
tools.boundary: No application server or per-site deployment is required.
tools.name: blog

thumb.alt: chat-webCLI: an on-device model selector and conversation interface.

line.out: a reply from a language model running on your own GPU

not.why: writes to a repository and publishes; this one keeps conversations in this browser and sends them nowhere

tools.limits: Needs WebGPU. Model weights are downloaded on first use. Conversations are saved in this browser's localStorage. No gate table yet.

params.name: prompt
params.description: The text prompt sent to the locally running model.

params.name: run
params.description: Run an on-device chat completion without a click.

params.name: model
params.description: One of the WebLLM model IDs offered by the app.

params.name: temperature
params.description: Number from 0 to 2; 0.7 by default.

tools.result: window.__webcli_result = { ok, op: 'chat', artifact: { mime: 'text/plain', name, size, dataUrl } | null, error: string | null, meta }
tools.boundary: A browser-based LLM chat app that runs large language models entirely in your browser using WebLLM and WebGPU - no server, no API keys, no data leaves your device.
tools.name: chat
chess

line.in: an invite link, or nothing for a game on this device
line.out: a game, with a PGN saved on this device if you choose

not.why: makes live calls; chess exchanges signed moves and can keep a game in a git repository

tools.limits: v0.2.0 (protocol 1). One network test passed; the wider real-device/network matrix, the real GitHub API path and the optional model on a real GPU remain unverified.
tools.egress: rooms: peers, relays and STUN; git-backed games: user-initiated GitHub commits
tools.boundary: On-device games are zero-egress. Rooms cannot be, because moves have to reach the other player; every request is declared and checkable in DevTools instead.

tools.name: drop

line.in: one or more files or folders from your device
line.out: verified files exchanged with the people in a temporary room

not.why: stores content for later; drop keeps both browsers present and transfers directly

tools.limits: v0.2.8 is functional for current desktop testing. Browser-size ceilings, throughput and the wider device matrix are pending.
tools.boundary: This is not storage, a cloud locker, a mailbox, or “AirDrop for the internet.” Both browsers must be open at the same time. There is no nearby discovery.

thumb.alt: dub-webCLI: subtitle input and timed speech controls.

line.out: one WAV with every cue spoken at its timestamp, and a report.json of overruns and collisions

not.why: turns speech into text; this only writes speech, and never time-stretches a cue

tools.limits: Byte-identical output holds on the wasm device with q8, not on webgpu. No run= surface yet.
tools.boundary: No uploads, no servers, no API keys. All processing happens locally in your browser using Transformers.js and ONNX Runtime WebAssembly.
tools.name: dub

thumb.alt: ffmpeg-webCLI: a video drop zone, trim sliders and operations for converting, resizing, extracting audio and GIF.

line.in: a video, audio or image file from your device
line.out: that media trimmed, converted, scaled or compressed, or as a GIF or extracted audio

not.why: only builds and manages adaptive-streaming libraries; this one is the general transforms

tools.limits: No gate table yet and no run= surface.
tools.boundary: No uploads, no servers -- all processing happens locally in your browser using WebAssembly.
tools.name: ffmpeg

line.in: an MP4 and the git repository it should live in
line.out: a versioned adaptive-streaming release (ladder, segments, playlists) committed and tagged name/vN

not.why: does general transforms and keeps nothing; this one does exactly one thing

tools.limits: Publishing is a commit to your repository, so it is egress, and it is yours to start. H.264 only; variable-frame-rate and rotated files are refused by name.
tools.boundary: No servers, no accounts, no uploads: your video is decoded and encoded in your browser, and nothing leaves it until you press Publish.
tools.name: hls

thumb.alt: look-webCLI: a VRM chooser and texture, material and blendshape editing tabs.

line.out: the same avatar, as a VRM, with its textures, materials, outfits or accessories changed

not.why: reads a face from a photo and binds it to a VRM; this one never sees a photo

tools.limits: The editor re-exports through its own writer, so the output is not a byte-audited edit of the input. Determinism is measured on the two bundled bases only.

params.name: vrm
params.description: URL of the VRM to edit.

params.name: run
params.description: Load the VRM and export it without a click.

result.shape: { ok, op: 'export', artifact: { mime, name, size, dataUrl } | null, error: string | null, meta: { source, bytesIn, bytesOut, vrmVersion } }

tools.boundary: It is not an installable offline PWA.
tools.name: look

thumb.alt: magick-webCLI: image input, processing controls and an output preview.

line.out: those images converted between 100+ formats, or edited with chained, batchable operations

not.why: edits the textures and materials of a VRM avatar; this one edits pictures and knows nothing of avatars

params.name: src
params.description: Image input URL(s), loaded with a credential-free GET.

params.name: run
params.description: One operation or conversion to run without a click.

params.name: params
params.description: JSON object containing operation parameters.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format; PNG is the default.

params.name: quality
params.description: Integer output quality from 1 to 100.

params.name: download
params.description: Click the download control automatically after success.

tools.result: window.__webcli_result = { ok, op, artifact: { mime, name, size, dataUrl } | null, error: string | null, meta }
tools.boundary: No uploads, no servers, all processing happens locally in your browser.
tools.name: magick

thumb.alt: portrait-webCLI: a face photo chooser, a base VRM picker and a Bind button.

line.in: a photo of one face and a base VRM
line.out: that VRM with its expressions bound to the face read from the photo

not.why: edits an avatar's textures and outfits by hand; this one reads a face, and its result is not a likeness

tools.limits: Approximate, not a likeness. One clear front-facing face. The photo is read from a local file only, so a run needs a person or a runner with the file.

params.name: vrm
params.description: Base VRM; defaults to the bundled male model.

params.name: run
params.description: Start the bind once a photo is supplied from local disk.

params.name: download
params.description: With run=bind, also save the result.

result.shape: { ok, op: 'bind', artifact: { mime, name, size, dataUrl } | null, error: string | null, meta }

tools.name: portrait

thumb.alt: rig-webCLI: character, motion and retargeting controls.

line.in: a skinned character (FBX, GLB or VRM) and motion files (BVH, FBX or GLB)
line.out: one optimized animated GLB carrying each motion as its own track

not.why: records motion from a camera; this one watches nothing and retargets motion that already exists

tools.limits: The optional in-page assist is off by default; turning it on downloads about 1 GB of model weights. Its tests are not yet published as a gate table.

params.name: character
params.description: URL of the character (FBX, GLB, VRM).

params.name: motion
params.description: URL of a BVH or face-record JSON; repeat for several tracks.

params.name: map
params.description: URL of a flat bone-map JSON.

params.name: args
params.description: Raw bake flags, e.g. "--fps 24 --trim 2:10".

params.name: run
params.description: Start the op as soon as the page loads.

result.shape: { ok, op: 'bake', artifact: { mime, name, size, dataUrl } | null, error: string | null, meta: { tracks, frames, fps, mapped, bones, units, blendshapes } }

tools.boundary: No uploads, no servers: everything happens in your browser.
tools.name: rig
rtc

line.in: an invite link, plus camera, microphone or screen when you choose to share them
line.out: a live peer-to-peer call; no file or artifact

not.why: exchanges signed game moves and offers; rtc sends live media between participants

tools.limits: v0.3.0 (protocol 3) has not yet been run on real devices. The latest recorded device run was on v0.2.0: two runs passed and one failed on one home Wi-Fi network.
tools.egress: user-initiated media to peers; signaling through relays and STUN
tools.boundary: A call has to send. Your media goes to the other people in the room, and the introduction relays and a STUN server are contacted to set that up.

thumb.alt: video-webCLI: media library, preview, timeline and export controls.

line.in: screen, camera, microphone or existing video clips
line.out: an edited MP4 with mixed audio and optional burned or selectable captions

not.why: records and assembles an editing timeline; ffmpeg transforms media files you already have

tools.limits: Capture is an explicit browser permission. Export determinism is not guaranteed across browser builds or hardware. No run= surface yet.
tools.boundary: A local-first iMovie-style editor that records, trims, captions and exports video without uploading it.
tools.name: video

thumb.alt: whisper-webCLI: audio transcription and subtitle controls.

line.in: an audio or video file from your device
line.out: a transcript as text, SRT or WebVTT

not.why: goes the other way, from subtitles to speech

tools.limits: No gate table yet and no run= surface. The Whisper model is downloaded on first use.
tools.boundary: No uploads, no servers. All processing happens locally in your browser using Transformers.js and ONNX models.
tools.name: whisper

libraries.name: 3DOM
libraries.description: A library for addressing and editing three.js scenes with CSS-like selectors, deterministic auto-labelling and undoable operations. It has no standalone tool UI or command surface.
libraries.boundary: No editor. No framework. No build step required. Just three.js (a peer dependency) and this.

libraries.name: only-connect
libraries.description: Shared browser-to-browser room transport used by drop, chess and rtc. Library only: it has no UI or command surface.
libraries.boundary: Guest Wi-Fi, classroom and institutional networks that isolate clients will still defeat a direct WebRTC connection. only-connect is the vehicle, not the cure.
